summary: Introductory discovery for Halcyon Bridge SaaS onramp. Customer evaluating Redwood for production inference for a multi-tenant SaaS (realtime recommendations + search). Primary concerns: VPC/private endpoints, KMS/encryption, predictable latency for 200–500 qps, and cost controls via batching and quantization recommendations. Agreed to run a pilot with baseline benchmarks and a security handoff. Next: share security docs, traffic profile, and schedule benchmark window.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-09 09:10 PT / 16:10 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Call link: zoom.us/j/xxxxx (recording available)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Halcyon Bridge CTO), Jon Peters (Head of Platform), Lei Zhang (Infra), Aisha Mohammed (Security)

[00:00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're excited to kick off this intro with Halcyon Bridge. quick round robin?
[00:00:07] Marta Ruiz: hi all, Marta here, CTO at Halcyon Bridge, we run the recommender and search infra for our SaaS tenants.
[00:00:12] Jon Peters: Jon, platform — focused on infra and scale.
[00:00:16] Lei Zhang: lei, infra eng, I run our k8s clusters and onprem connections.
[00:00:20] Aisha Mohammed: Aisha, security lead — I'll be handling compliance questions.
[00:00:25] Alex Chen: great, priya and samir from our side will go more into the technical bits. just to set agenda: we want to understand your workload, constraints, success criteria and then map Redwood options — hosted, dedicated, private — to those.

[00:00:40] Priya Kapoor: quick clarifying q: are you primarily looking for hosted API to start or private/VPC?
[00:00:46] Jon Peters: our preference is private VPC peering or private endpoint — we have tenant data residency concerns, can't send certain PII to public endpoints. but we want to avoid full onprem ops if possible.
[00:00:58] Alex Chen: totally. we do private deployment with customer-controlled VPC and an optional private control plane. that gives devs the same API but traffic stays over the peered network.

[00:01:10] Marta Ruiz: good. throughput: average 200 qps, burst to 500 qps during business hours. tail latency needs to be under 150ms 95th for short prompts — our recommender path is time sensitive.
[00:01:23] Priya Kapoor: helpful — couple follow ups: prompt lengths, token counts, and whether you're doing streaming responses?
[00:01:29] Lei Zhang: typical prompt is 40–70 tokens, 1–3-shot few examples, responses 30–120 tokens. some routes are streaming, yes, for real-time UI.

[00:01:40] Samir Patel: ok. for that profile we'd consider a dedicated pool or private with dedicated capacity to meet SLOs. hosted can work but you'd likely pay more or see variable p95 unless we reserve capacity.

[00:01:55] Marta Ruiz: how does caching play? our current system tries to prefix cache but it's messy.
[00:02:00] Priya Kapoor: we support prefix and KV cache — automatic prefix caching reduces tokens and latency if you have repeated prefixes. spelled out in our docs. note: transcription may say K-V case sometimes, hehe

[00:02:12] Aisha Mohammed: security questions: do you support customer KMS integration and HSM-backed keys? we also need audit logs for every tokenized request for compliance.
[00:02:20] Alex Chen: yes — KMS integration is supported for private deployments; we can integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or bring-your-own HSM through our private control plane. audit logs and immutable request traces are available and exportable to your SIEM. we can share the SOC2 pack after the call.

[00:02:36] Jon Peters: latency vs cost question — our finance team will push back on big reserved commitments. any levers besides reserved capacity?
[00:02:43] Priya Kapoor: yes batching and quantization guidance are the primary levers. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantized model variants that reduce GPU memory and cost. also intelligent batching with latency SLOs — you can set per-route latency targets and we'll balance batching to meet SLOs while improving token efficiency.

[00:02:58] Lei Zhang: quantization — is that automatic or manual tuning? we worry about quality regressions.
[00:03:03] Samir Patel: good question — we recommend model/quantization pairs based on evals. Redwood Optimize will run quality regressions on your prompt sets; we have guardrails and will show metric deltas, you can opt into a quantized variant for particular routes.

[00:03:20] Marta Ruiz: we also want the option to fallback to smaller models during incidents to preserve latency and availability. how does routing/fallback work?
[00:03:27] Priya Kapoor: smart routing policies — you can configure primary model, fallback model, region fallback. When capacity or latency thresholds are hit, requests can be routed to a compatible variant. we can demo automatic fallback behaviors.

[00:03:40] Jon Peters: networking specifics: do you require an agent in our VPC? any egress rules?
[00:03:45] Alex Chen: for private deployment we deploy customer-managed nodes in your VPC or on-prem. We can also do VPC peering with private endpoints. Egress rules are minimal; most calls stay inbound from your apps to the private endpoint. we'll share a network diagram.

[00:03:57] Aisha Mohammed: data residency — can we pin models to specific regions and ensure logs stay in-region?
[00:04:02] Priya Kapoor: yes, region pinning is supported. Audit logs can be kept in your region and integrated with your logging stack. retention is configurable per contract.

[00:04:12] Marta Ruiz: benchmarks — we need a baseline to compare to our existing infra (MajorCloudX). can Redwood run end-to-end benchmarks with our test workload?
[00:04:20] Samir Patel: absolutely. typical pilot: you provide traffic profile and a small corpus of prompts; we run a 24–48 hour benchmark using a reserved pool sized to your QPS and measure p50/p95/p99, token cost, and throughput. we'll include KV cache and batching on/off comparisons.

[00:04:35] Jon Peters: good. what about tenancy model — we are multi-tenant SaaS, want strict tenant isolation for embeddings and vector DBs. any best practices?
[00:04:44] Priya Kapoor: we recommend tenant-scoped model instances and per-tenant routing keys; embeddings can be stored in your managed vector DB — we integrate with our dedicated private deployment to ensure keys never leave your VPC. also RBAC at the API/key level so you can segment by tenant.

[00:04:58] Lei Zhang: about the vector workflow: you mention integrated caching and streaming; do you support sticky sessions for KV caches to reduce cold starts?
[00:05:05] Samir Patel: yes, KV cache warmup and sticky routing help keep cache warm for hot tenants. we can configure warmup triggers and pre-load frequent prefixes.

[00:05:15] Marta Ruiz: rough pricing framing — are we looking at percent savings vs cloud provider if we go dedicated?
[00:05:20] Alex Chen: depends on model choice and utilization. Dedicated pools with autoscaling and reserved capacity usually lower unit cost vs pure hosted bursty usage. We'll provide a tailored cost model after we see your traffic histogram — that's why the traffic export is important.

[00:05:34] Aisha Mohammed: compliance — do you run internal pen tests and provide evidence for SOC2?
[00:05:39] Alex Chen: yes, SOC2 Type II available, pen test reports are possible under NDA, and we provide control mappings for common frameworks. I'll include the pack in the follow-up.

[00:05:50] Jon Peters: integrations — our stack uses an internal API gateway and service-mesh. what integration points do you expose?
[00:05:56] Priya Kapoor: REST + gRPC endpoints, streaming websockets, and SDKs. You can front Redwood with your gateway — we usually recommend routing policies at the edge and tokenized keys per route.

[00:06:06] Marta Ruiz: timeline — if we start pilot, how long to baseline? weeks? months?
[00:06:10] Samir Patel: typical pilot is 4–6 weeks including setup, benchmarks, and a short evaluation. If you want a smaller proof-of-value (just benchmarks), we can do that in 2 weeks once we have traffic and access.

[00:06:22] Lei Zhang: what access do you need for pilot? credentials? staging endpoints?
[00:06:25] Alex Chen: we need service account for hitting the private endpoint or peering config, sample prompt set, and traffic profile. Minimal infra changes required if you choose hosted; private will need VPC peering or agent deploy.

[00:06:36] Aisha Mohammed: are you ok with an external audit during pilot? customer auditors might want to run a scan.
[00:06:40] Alex Chen: yes, under NDA we can coordinate scans and provide remediation timelines.

[00:06:45] Jon Peters: any known blockers for hybrid onprem connectors? we have some air-gapped components.
[00:06:50] Priya Kapoor: for air-gapped we offer an on-prem package; syncs to control plane can be done via offline artifacts. there is additional ops work but it's supported. we'll detail the on-prem runbook in the security pack.

[00:07:02] Marta Ruiz: ok let's talk concrete next steps. we want to see the SOC2, network diagram, and an SOW for a 2-week benchmark and a 6-week pilot option.
[00:07:11] Alex Chen: noted — action: we'll send SOC2 + network diagram + pilot SOW. Priya will draft benchmark plan.

[00:07:18] Priya Kapoor: I'll also propose the model list — e.g., one large open model and a quantized variant for cost comparison. Also include test harness for streaming vs non-streaming.

[00:07:26] Lei Zhang: we'll get you the traffic histograms and prompt sets; can we have a shared drive link?
[00:07:30] Alex Chen: yes i'll create a shared folder in drive and upload items.

[00:07:35] Marta Ruiz: any competitors you work with in parallel? we're also talking to MajorCloudX and EdgeGrid — just so you know.
[00:07:41] Alex Chen: understood — we'll include benchmark metrics to compare.

[00:07:45] Jon Peters: question: are you able to do controlled fault injection during pilot to test graceful degradation?
[00:07:50] Samir Patel: yes — we can run scenario tests: model fallback, region failover, cold KV cache, and measure end-to-end SLOs. we'll include that in the benchmark plan.

[00:07:58] Aisha Mohammed: please also include data retention and log deletion policies for the pilot in the security doc.
[00:08:03] Alex Chen: will do.

[00:08:06] (long pause, background noise)
[00:08:20] Alex Chen: ok last bit, timeline recap: Alex to send security pack + network diagram + SOW by 6/11; Lei to send traffic/profile 6/12; Priya to provide benchmark plan 6/15; target benchmark window week of 6/22. follow-up meeting to lock pilot start by 6/18.

[00:08:36] Marta Ruiz: sounds good, thanks.
[00:08:38] Jon Peters: thanks everyone.
[00:08:40] Alex Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up.

[00:08:45] Transcript notes: occasional transcription artifacts (K V case vs KV cache, quantaization). References shared: quickstart guide (redwood.com/docs/quickstart), security pack placeholder (link to be shared), pilot SOW template (internal).

End of transcript.
